description.narrative: The development objectives of the Environmental Pollution Abatement Project for Lebanon are to assist the Borrower in: (a) reducing industrial pollution in targeted industrial enterprises; and (b) strengthening the monitoring and enforcement capabilities of the Ministry of Environment (MOE). The project comprises two components. The first component on technical assistance aims to strengthen through technical support and training the capacity of MOE, the banking sector and the industrial associations, and provide project management support. The second component on investment sub-projects aims to provide concessional loans through the banking sector for pollution control to an estimated 20 to 25 public and private enterprises in order to bring air emissions, effluent discharges, and industrial waste generation towards compliance with national environmental standards in a cost-effective manner. This component will consist of a credit facility to provide sub-loans of at least US$100,000 per enterprise to implement pollution control projects and thereby reduce pollution load.

The development objectives of the project are to assist the Borrower in: (a) reducing industrial pollution in targeted Industrial Enterprises; and (b) strengthening the monitoring and enforcement capabilities of the MOE.

title.narrative: Industrial solid waste reduced under the project in the targeted enterprises

comment.narrative: <p>The rendering plant of Wilco PM is the only LEPAP sub-project addressing solid waste and is currently operated in batches. The rendering plant is operated 1 day/week while the slaughtering lines are operated 5 days/week, and as such, it is covering the waste generated during one day of production only. A rendering expert was recruited by the project to assess the operation s of the rendering plant and facilitate the marketing of the end-products.</p>

title.narrative: Guidelines and tools for environmental monitoring/compliance for specific industrial sectors developed

comment.narrative: <p>The target was 133% achieved. The 12 Guidelines prepared covering the following sectors: Slaughterhouse, Meat processing, Dairy Industry, Cattle Farm, Cement Mixing, Asphalt Mixing, Stone Cutting, Cement Blocks, paints, paper and cardboard, beverages and cement. </p>

title.narrative: Sub-loans issued to enterprises for pollution reduction

comment.narrative: <p>The target was 87% achieved. The figured does not include one sub-loan that was issued, but the project was cancelled before any funds were used.</p>

title.narrative: People trained on environmental compliance/ monitoring/ enforcement and awareness

comment.narrative:
<p>The target was 328% achieved. 11 trainings were conducted, covering the following topics: Sustainable Management of Industrial Areas, Implementation modality for BDL Memo #265/2014 and #382/2015, industrial hazardous waste, Implementation of Decision 189 dated 13/4/2016, environ mental compliance of Category I Industries, Industrial Wastewater Treatment for Pulp and Paper Industries, LEPAP eligibility Criteria & World Bank Environmental and Social Safeguards, Industrial Wastewater Treatment for Paints Industries, Wstewater Monitoring, World Bank Occupational health & Safety and Grievance Redress Mechanisms, and Industrial Wastewater Treatment for Food Industries. Participants were affiliated with the following organizations: MoE, MoI, AICS, UNDP, municipaliti es, ALI, representatives of existing/planned industrial areas, commercial banks, CDR, MoF, MoH, MoIM, OMSAR, Consulting firms, Industrial establishments, Contractors, UNIDO, FCCIA, NGOs, Universities, Syndicates, LEPAP Advisory Committee Members, Industrial Establishments, IRI, BdL, Water & Wastewater Establishments, Environmental Laboratories, and MoPH.</p>
<p>Indicator was revised in the 2018 retructuring. Original indicator was "people trained".</p>
<p>The target was 150% achieved. Participating banks were Audi, Fransabank, Byblos, Bank Med, BLF, and BEMO.</p>

title.narrative: BOD/COD reduction achieved under the project in the targeted enterprises

comment.narrative: <p>???????The WWTPs of Kassatly Chtaura, Chateau Ksara, Sicomo and Libanlait (first wave) have been operational since before the time of project closing. Latest third-party testing results show a reduction in BOD from 8.8 tons/d to 1.2 tons/day with a resulting efficiency of 85.23%. The total load of COD before treatment is 14,1 tons/d and the total COD reduction achieved is 10.76 tons/d equivalent to a treatment efficiency of 76.18%. A fifth WWTP sub-project, Hawa Chicken, had completed the LEPAP-funded portion of its sub-project at the time of project closing, but the plant was not operational until September 2023, and its results are therefore not included in this BOD/COD reduction outcome.</p>

title.narrative: Enterprises that benefit from LEPAP environmental services

comment.narrative: <p>The target was 175% achieved. Environmental services included preparation of Environmental Impact Assessments; assessment of environmental status and provision of recommendations on appropriate mitigation measures; environmental audits; Assessment of wastewater generation; Procurement and assessment of offers, e.g., for WWTPs; ESMP preparation; feasibility assessments; Preparation of a Compliance Action Plans; Odors mapping and suggestion of odor control and treatment plan; Development of Health and Safety Assessment; Assessment of rendering end-products usages and markets.</p>

title.narrative: Enterprises financed through the project aiming towards the environmental compliance Decree no. 8471-2012

comment.narrative:
<p>Nine enterprises borrowed under LEPAP (reaching 90% of target), with 11 financed sub-projects (Cimenterie Nationale, Wilco PM, Sicomo, Kassatly Chtaura, Ciment de Sibline, Libanlait, Zinaline, Chateau Ksara, Hawa Chicken). All subprojects were completed and operated or commissioned before the time of project closure, except for Hawa Chicken, which had completed the LEPAP-funded portion of its work, but only became operational in September 2023.</p>
<p>Revised in 2018 restructuring - original indicator was "Enterprises financed through the project that conform to the environmental compliance decree (8471-2012)". </p>

title.narrative: Particulate Matter reduction achieved under the project in the targeted enterprises

comment.narrative: <p>All 5 LEPAP sub-projects addressing air pollution are operational. This indicator takes into account the subprojects implem ented at the following industries: Cimenterie Nationale, Zinaline, Sicomo and Ciment de Sibline. The stack measurements for Ci menterie Nationale and Sicomo data is collected from online monitoring systems and for Zinaline and Ciment de Sibline it is an estimation of the emissions and flow rate of the extraction system. The total dust emissions before the implementation of the sub-projects was around 594 kilo tons/y and the total emissions reduction is equivalent to 546 kt/y (~ 91.9%).</p>

title.narrative: Industrial database including monitoring, permitting, and enforcement data operational

comment.narrative: <p>Database has been completed, therefore the target is 100% achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in number of non-compliant operational enterprises addressed in letters from MOE to Ministry of Industry, Ministry of Interior, governors, municipalities, and prosecutors

comment.narrative: <p>Baseline 2017: 62 letters. Total letters issued from January 2018 till January 2023 is estimated to be around 210 letters (339% achieved). Examples of non-compliance letters include: complaints submitted to MoE against industries related to pollution which ha ve been processed by MoE, MoE Letters issued to MoI, governors, etc. to respond to industrial pollution related matters.</p>
